newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Dlr seen eclipsing recent multiyear peaks.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Dlr seen eclipsing recent multiyear peaks.

text.p: The dollar stands just below its recent 56-month high against the yen and 38-month peak versus the mark, and technical analysts said they see little to stop the greenback from punching through those levels.
Dollar/yen is closer to the prize than dollar/mark, having come within two-hundredths of a yen of the 127.16 yen high from April 10 in Wednesday's U.S. trade.

"We've had three higher lows over the last three (trading) days and each time the dollar has come back to retest 127. That's a bullish signal," said Martin Autotte, technical analyst at CIBC Wood Gundy in Montreal.
While dollar/yen traded within a tight range of less than half a yen on Wednesday, chartists said the solid support near 126.50 should enable an upside break in the near future.

"I do expect new highs above 127.14 (yen), and once that's confirmed, I'm pretty confident it will get to the 128 to 128.35 zone," said Pete Grant, senior foreign exchange analyst at MMS International in Chicago.

Dollar/yen met resistance near 127 as an overnight drop in mark/yen helped weigh on the dollar. Mark/yen is forming a triangle, which should encouarge technical buying in coming sessions, technicians said.
"I would probably put a slight emphasis on buying strategies," Grant said.
Chartists said current mark/yen supports rest near 73, 72.75, 72.60 and 72.40. On the topside, resistance appears at 73.60 and 74.

Dollar/mark came close to an outside reversal on Wednesday, but failed to hold above Tuesday's high at 1.7326, chartists noted. The greenback had earlier posted a lower low at 1.7205 marks, surpassing Tuesday's trough near 1.7220.
"On a technical basis, (dollar/mark) looks very strong," Autotte said.
"We saw a new high near 1.74 marks on Monday and we are on our way to a retest of that level. It will probably be exceeded by the end of the week," Autotte added.

Above 1.74 marks, the dollar could target a fibonnaci retracement level at 1.7510, Grant said. That level would represent a 150-percent retracement of the bear phase that dropped the greenback to 1.6610 on March 31 from a peak at 1.7210 on March 6, he noted.
